userStories.title: Add Core Web Vitals optimization: hero image priority and lazy-loading
userStories.description: The Hero component (Hero.tsx) likely uses a large banner image that is the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) element. Without the `priority` prop on the Next.js Image component, the hero image is lazy-loaded, causing LCP scores above 4s on mobile — a Google ranking signal. Additionally, below-fold images should be explicitly lazy-loaded and sized with the `sizes` attribute to prevent Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). Target: LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1.
acceptanceCriteria: Hero image uses <Image priority> prop (no lazy loading on LCP element)

Reference: https://blog.kieranroberts.dev/http-security-headers-and-how-to-set-them-in-nextjs

userStories.title: Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) header
userStories.description: No Content Security Policy exists on the site, leaving it vulnerable to XSS and code injection attacks. A CSP for a static/SSG Next.js site can be configured without nonces via next.config.ts, whitelisting self, inline styles, and the specific third-party domains actually used (e.g. booking proxy). This is a layered defense on top of basic security headers.
acceptanceCriteria: CSP header present on all HTML page responses
default-src 'self' is the base policy
script-src allows 'self' and whitelisted third parties (e.g. googletagmanager.com if used)
frame-ancestors restricts embedding to same origin
img-src allows 'self', blob:, data:, and ak-d.tripcdn.com (already used for remote images)
CSP does not block any existing site functionality (no console CSP errors)
Policy validated with Google CSP Evaluator tool
technicalNotes: Since the site uses static/ISR rendering, use the without-nonces approach via next.config.ts headers()
Must whitelist admin.pelangicapsulehostel.com for the /book proxy rewrite
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/content-security-policy
Use upgrade-insecure-requests directive to enforce HTTPS
dependencies: Add HTTP security headers to next.config.ts

userStories.title: Add LodgingBusiness schema: checkinTime, checkoutTime, availableLanguage, petsAllowed
userStories.description: The existing Hostel schema in StructuredData.tsx is missing several LodgingBusiness-specific properties that Google uses for hotel knowledge panels and rich results: checkinTime/checkoutTime (already in the data layer but not in schema), availableLanguage (EN/ZH), petsAllowed, and numberOfRooms. These properties are required for full LodgingBusiness rich result eligibility.
acceptanceCriteria: checkinTime: 'T14:00' and checkoutTime: 'T12:00' are added using ISO 8601 Time format
availableLanguage array includes Language objects for English and Chinese
petsAllowed: false is explicitly declared
numberOfRooms is populated with actual pod count
Updated schema validates without errors in Google Rich Results Test
starRating property is absent (hostel has no official star rating body)
technicalNotes: checkinTime/checkoutTime accept ISO 8601 Time values like 'T14:00:00'
availableLanguage uses Language type: {"@type": "Language", "name": "English"}
Reference: https://schema.org/LodgingBusiness
Reference: https://schema.org/docs/hotels.html

userStories.title: Remove or replace first-party AggregateRating in StructuredData.tsx
userStories.description: The current StructuredData.tsx embeds a hardcoded AggregateRating with ratingValue: '4.9' and ratingCount: '500' directly on the hostel's own website. Google's structured data guidelines explicitly prohibit first-party self-declared reviews for rich result eligibility — this risks a manual action or loss of star review features in SERPs.
acceptanceCriteria: The hardcoded AggregateRating block is removed from the self-hosted Hostel schema OR replaced with a clearly attributed third-party source
If removed, no AggregateRating property exists in any self-hosted schema on the same entity
Site does not receive a Google Search Console 'Structured data' manual action warning
The visual 4.9/5 star rating in Reviews.tsx component is unaffected (it is UI, not schema)
technicalNotes: Google policy: 'If the entity being reviewed controls the reviews, pages are ineligible for star review features'
Reference: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/review-snippet
Alternative: embed a third-party review widget (Hostelworld, Booking.com) and use their schema
The Reviews.tsx component currently shows curated hardcoded reviews — this is UI-only and acceptable

userStories.title: Add skip navigation link and ARIA landmarks for keyboard accessibility (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.1)
userStories.description: The site currently has no skip navigation link, meaning keyboard and screen reader users must tab through the entire header on every page load. WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks) requires a mechanism to skip repeated navigation. The EU European Accessibility Act (EAA) mandates compliance for websites serving EU customers from June 2025.
acceptanceCriteria: A visually hidden 'Skip to main content' link is the first focusable element on every page
The skip link becomes visible when focused (not permanently hidden)
The skip link targets an element with id='main-content' or role='main'
All major page sections use semantic HTML5 landmarks: <header>, <nav>, <main>, <footer>
All interactive elements are reachable and operable via keyboard alone
Focus indicators are visible on all interactive elements
technicalNotes: Implement in layout.tsx as first child of <body>
Use Tailwind sr-only class with focus:not-sr-only focus:absolute for visible-on-focus pattern
Reference: https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/

userStories.title: Optimize INP (Interaction to Next Paint) for booking and filter interactions
userStories.description: INP replaced FID as a Core Web Vital in March 2024 and measures responsiveness to all user interactions. The blog category filter, booking bar, and chat widget are likely sources of long tasks inflating INP on mobile. Poor INP (>200ms) negatively impacts Google ranking. The existing CWV work only addressed LCP and lazy-loading, not interaction responsiveness.
acceptanceCriteria: INP score is 200ms or below at the 75th percentile as measured by Chrome UX Report or Vercel Speed Insights
No single user interaction triggers a JavaScript task longer than 50ms
The blog category filter interaction completes visual update within 200ms on mid-range Android device
Heavy client components (ChatWidget, MobileBookingBar) are wrapped in dynamic import with loading skeleton
INP measured before and after implementation showing improvement
technicalNotes: Use next/dynamic with ssr: false for ChatWidget and MobileBookingBar to reduce initial JS bundle
Break up long event handlers with scheduler.yield() or setTimeout(0) where applicable
Reference: https://web.dev/articles/inp

userStories.title: Add AVIF/WebP format support and responsive sizes prop to gallery images
userStories.description: The Gallery.tsx component may serve unoptimised images without the sizes prop, causing Next.js to generate fixed 1x/2x descriptors instead of a full responsive srcset. AVIF compresses 20% smaller than WebP and reduces image payload by 60-80%, directly improving LCP and data usage for mobile users on Malaysian mobile networks.
acceptanceCriteria: All gallery images use the Next.js component (not plain tags)
All <Image> components include a sizes prop appropriate to layout (e.g. '(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 33vw')
next.config.ts includes formats: ['image/avif', 'image/webp'] in the images config
Chrome DevTools Network tab shows .avif or .webp files served to supporting browsers
Lighthouse image audit shows no 'Serve images in next-gen formats' warning for gallery images
technicalNotes: Add formats: ['image/avif', 'image/webp'] to the images block in next.config.ts
The sizes prop is required for responsive srcset generation; without it Next.js generates only 1x/2x fixed descriptors
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/components/image

userStories.title: Add language switcher UI component with NEXT_LOCALE cookie persistence
userStories.description: Hreflang tags have been added for EN/ZH-CN but there is no visible language switcher for users. Chinese travellers from Singapore and China represent a significant portion of JB hostel guests. A language switcher that sets the NEXT_LOCALE cookie ensures preference persists across sessions and is the prerequisite UI before any translated content can be deployed.
acceptanceCriteria: A language switcher (EN | 中文) is visible in the Header component
Clicking 中文 sets NEXT_LOCALE=zh cookie and shows a 'Chinese version coming soon' toast if translations don't exist yet
Clicking EN sets NEXT_LOCALE=en
The current active language is visually indicated
The switcher is accessible: keyboard operable and has aria-label='Language selector'
The cookie is set with SameSite=Lax per Next.js i18n documentation
technicalNotes: Next.js NEXT_LOCALE cookie takes priority over Accept-Language header
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/guides/internationalization
Can initially render as a static UI with the ZH option showing toast 'Chinese version coming soon'
Use URL subdirectory pattern /zh/ when translations are ready

userStories.title: Add 'Book Direct' benefits section to /book page for conversion uplift
userStories.description: The /book page proxies the booking engine but lacks visible 'book direct' trust signals. Research shows that hospitality sites displaying direct booking benefits (best price guarantee, direct support, flexible cancellation) see 10-22% improvement in direct conversion rates. The surrounding page wrapper is rendered by Next.js and can be enhanced without touching the proxied booking widget.
acceptanceCriteria: A 'Why Book Direct?' section is visible above or alongside the booking widget on /book
Section includes at least 3 concrete direct-booking benefits (e.g. Best Rate Guarantee, Free WhatsApp support, Flexible cancellation)
Section includes at least one trust badge or security indicator
A comparison callout showing OTA commission savings vs direct price is present
Section is mobile-responsive and does not obscure the booking widget CTA on small screens
technicalNotes: The /book route is a rewrite to admin.pelangicapsulehostel.com — the surrounding page wrapper is rendered by Next.js
Reference: https://spiltmilkwebdesign.com/conversion-rate-optimization-website-ux-for-boutique-hotels-in-2025/

userStories.title: Add PDPA/GDPR cookie consent banner for analytics compliance
userStories.description: If the site uses Google Analytics or any tracking pixels, Malaysia's Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) requires explicit user consent before loading non-essential cookies. The EU GDPR applies to EU visitors. Currently there is no consent mechanism on the site, creating a legal compliance gap as the hostel attracts international visitors.
acceptanceCriteria: A cookie consent banner appears on first visit for users who have not yet consented
Banner offers Accept All and Reject Non-Essential options at minimum
Non-essential scripts (analytics, tracking) are not loaded until the user accepts
Consent choice is stored in a cookie and the banner does not re-appear on subsequent visits
Banner is keyboard accessible and screen reader friendly (role='dialog', aria-label)
Consent state is respected on all pages
technicalNotes: Use client-side cookie reading to keep pages statically generated (no SSR performance hit)
Reference: https://posthog.com/tutorials/nextjs-cookie-banner
Libraries: react-cookie-consent or CookieYes SaaS embed are both viable options

userStories.title: Add dedicated /amenities page with full LocationFeatureSpecification schema
userStories.description: Amenities content is currently only in the homepage Amenities.tsx component. A dedicated /amenities page with expanded content (Wi-Fi speed, co-working details, laundry, kitchen rules) creates a new indexable URL capturing digital-nomad and long-stay search queries. Full LocationFeatureSpecification objects in JSON-LD enable Google's amenities panel in hotel rich results.
acceptanceCriteria: /amenities page exists and returns HTTP 200
Page has generateMetadata with target keywords (e.g. 'free WiFi hostel JB', 'co-working hostel Johor Bahru')
Page includes a complete amenity list with icons, descriptions, and relevant caveats (e.g. WiFi speed, kitchen hours)
JSON-LD on the page includes expanded amenityFeature array with all amenities as LocationFeatureSpecification
Page is linked from the homepage Amenities section and the site Footer
Page is added to sitemap.ts
technicalNotes: LocationFeatureSpecification requires name and value (boolean or string) properties
Reference: https://schema.org/LodgingBusiness (amenityFeature property)
Target audience: digital nomads searching for co-working hostels near Singapore
Example: {"@type": "LocationFeatureSpecification", "name": "Free WiFi", "value": true}

userStories.title: Add Google Sustainability Attributes and eco-friendly content section
userStories.description: Google Business Profile for hotels supports sustainability attributes, and 82% of travellers say sustainability influences their booking decisions. Adding a sustainability section to the website and corresponding GBP attributes signals relevance for the growing 'sustainable travel' search segment, increasingly weighted in Google's 2025 hotel profile algorithm.
acceptanceCriteria: A brief sustainability/eco-friendly section (minimum one paragraph) exists on the About or /amenities page
Content mentions at least 2 verifiable eco practices (e.g. water dispensers to reduce plastic bottles, LED lighting, recycling bins)
Google Business Profile sustainability attributes are documented as an offline task to action
The website content references the hostel's actual practices — no fabricated claims
Section is linked from the homepage or Footer if standalone
technicalNotes: GBP sustainability attributes are set in Google Business Profile dashboard under 'Attributes'
Reference: https://gmbapi.com/news/optimising-google-business-profiles-for-hotels-with-new-features/
No schema.org type currently exists specifically for sustainability; use plain content + GBP attributes
